title: Microsoft Teams: reactions in events with up to 100,000 attendees
summary: Hold: the page incorrectly reports license-assignment automation as undocumented, although Microsoft documents assigning Teams add-on licenses through PowerShell and Microsoft Graph. The roadmap facts, current reactions ceiling, licensing requirements and printed policy controls are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans reactions in Teams events with up to 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Teams now supports reactions in events at this scale.

claims.claim: Attendees will be able to send reactions and see reactions others send.
claims.quote: You can send reactions during the event and see the reactions others send, so everyone can share the moment together.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; changes; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Current documentation limits event reactions to events with up to 20,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Available only for events with up to 20,000 attendees and can't be enabled for a subset of participants (for example, only the first 20,000 attendees) in larger events.

claims.claim: For events with 20,001 to 100,000 attendees, reactions are off in the scheduling form and organisers cannot turn them on today.
claims.quote: For events with 20,001 to 100,000 attendees, this feature is turned off in the scheduling form and can't be turned on by organizers.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the new 100,000-attendee reactions behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 100000 town hall reactions tenant events policy default AllowMeetingReactions. Opened manage-reactions-meetings and meetings-events-feature-comparison; the latter still limits reactions to 20,000.

claims.claim: The reactions default is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Reactions.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit. ... Under Meeting engagement, turn the Reactions toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMeetingReactions $false sets reactions off using MicrosoftTeams PowerShell.
claims.quote: [-Identity] <XdsIdentity> ... [-AllowMeetingReactions <Boolean>] ... Set to false to disable Meeting Reactions.

claims.claim: The existing meeting reactions setting defaults to On in organisers' Meeting options.
claims.quote: By default, meeting reactions are set to On in your organizers' Meeting options.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The meeting policy sets a default for meetings and events, and organisers can change reactions per meeting or event rather than being subject to an enforced block.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can use the Teams admin center or PowerShell to set the default value for reactions in your organizers' Meeting options. Organizers can change the setting for each meeting and event they create.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default specifically for the new reactions capability above 20,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 100000 town hall reactions tenant events policy default AllowMeetingReactions. Read roadmap, manage-reactions-meetings, meetings-events-feature-comparison and events-licensing; none specifies the future above-20,000 arrival default.

claims.claim: No separate tenant-wide or events-policy reactions switch for events above 20,000 attendees is documented in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 100000 town hall reactions tenant events policy default AllowMeetingReactions. Opened manage-reactions-meetings and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy syntax; no separate large-event reactions parameter appears.

claims.claim: Town hall creation is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers with the policy from creating town halls.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.claim: Attendee access is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests restricts town hall access to the organisation and guests.
claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization and guests to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests

claims.claim: Who can attend events optimized for a large audience defaults to Everyone.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone.

claims.claim: The attendee-access policy applies to large-audience events created by organisers assigned that policy.
claims.quote: Controls who can attend events optimized for large audiences (such as town halls) created by organizers with this policy.

claims.claim: Assign attendee packs at Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Assign to new users > Attendee pack.
claims.quote: On the Licenses tab, select Assign to new users to get started. ... In the Assign Add-on licenses pane ... For each individual user, select the pack size that you want to assign in the Attendee pack column.
claims.fix: Use 'Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Assign to new users > Assign Add-on licenses > Attendee pack'; the omitted pane heading is not a navigation choice.

claims.claim: Automation for assigning Attendee Capacity Pack add-on licenses to organisers is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to. ... POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense
claims.fix: Replace controls[4].api null with kind 'graph', call 'POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/user-assignlicense?view=graph-rest-1.0'. Add to the note: 'The request body uses addLicenses with the purchased pack skuId; removeLicenses is required and can be empty. This is the general user-license assignment API.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-add-on-licensing/assign-teams-add-on-licenses, which documents PowerShell assignment for Teams add-on licenses; its SKU table explicitly says it is partial.

claims.claim: Managing attendee-pack assignments in the Teams admin center requires Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Global Administrator role to access the License Management section and manage all licensing capabilities in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Teams Administrator has read-only access to attendee-pack License Management in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Users assigned the Teams Administrator role can access the License Management section in read-only mode and cannot create, modify, or remove license assignments or settings.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Large-event capacity is licensed through Attendee Capacity Pack add-ons for Teams Enterprise.
claims.quote: Teams Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licenses for Teams Enterprise that let event organizers host events for up to 100,000 attendees.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[4].governs; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Events above 3,000 attendees with engagement capabilities require purchased Attendee Capacity Pack licenses, subject to the stated legacy Premium exception.
claims.quote: To host events with more than 3,000 attendees with engagement capabilities (chat, reactions, raise hand, polls, Q&A), organizations must purchase Attendee Capacity Pack add-on licenses and assign them to organizers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[4]
claims.claim: Attendee packs are assigned to the event organiser, not every attendee.
claims.quote: organizations must purchase Attendee Capacity Pack add-on licenses and assign them to organizers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Attendee packs enable event capacity up to 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Attendee packs enable events with up to 100,000 attendees.

claims.claim: The available pack sizes are 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 35,000, 50,000, 75,000 and 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: They can be purchased to support 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 35,000, 50,000, 75,000, and 100,000 event attendees.

claims.claim: An organiser can hold only one attendee pack at a time.
claims.quote: While your organization can purchase multiple packs, each organizer can only be assigned one pack.

claims.claim: Attendee packs increase capacity but do not unlock other feature capabilities.
claims.quote: Attendee packs increase capacity for Teams events. They don't unlock any other feature capabilities.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: An active Teams Premium license bought before 1 April 2026 retains event capacity of up to 100,000 until its current term ends.
claims.quote: Organizers with an active Teams Premium license purchased before April 1, 2026, can continue to host events for up to 100,000 attendees until their current Teams Premium term ends.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An event above 20,000 attendees needs at least the 35,000 pack or the active legacy Premium entitlement described on the page.
claims.quote: They can be purchased to support 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 35,000, 50,000, 75,000, and 100,000 event attendees. ... The attendee capacities included with Teams Enterprise and an attendee pack aren't combined.

claims.quote: Searched: reactions 100,000 latency default billing; Teams reactions 100000 attendees names sender emoji stream latency price meter. Opened events-licensing, attendee-capacity-pack and manage-reactions-meetings; none names a reactions meter.

claims.quote: Searched: Attendee Capacity Pack price. Opened attendee-capacity-pack and attendee-capacity-pack-manage in full; neither publishes pack prices.

claims.claim: No separate license specific to the reactions capacity increase is published.
claims.quote: Searched: reactions 100,000 latency default billing; Attendee Capacity Pack price. Read events-licensing, attendee-capacity-pack and manage-reactions-meetings; they name general event entitlement, not a separate reactions-expansion license.

claims.claim: The described reactions are sent by attendees, not autonomous actions.
